questions.question: What is the fundamental rule regarding the 'id' attribute in an HTML document?
options: An ID must only contain numbers
An ID must be strictly unique within the entire HTML document
An ID must match the element tag name
An ID cannot be longer than 8 characters
questions.explanation: The 'id' attribute must be unique across the document; duplicate IDs violate HTML specifications.

questions.question: How are custom data attributes named in HTML5?
options: Using the data- prefix (e.g., data-user-id)
Using the custom: prefix
Using the attr- prefix
Using the meta_ prefix
questions.explanation: Custom data attributes must begin with 'data-' followed by lowercase characters.

questions.question: If an element has data-product-price="49", how is it accessed in JavaScript?
options: element.dataProductPrice
element.dataset.productPrice
element.getData('product-price')
element.customData.price
questions.hint: The dataset property converts names to camelCase.
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, data attributes are accessible on the element's 'dataset' object in camelCase: element.dataset.productPrice.

questions.question: What effect does the hidden boolean attribute have on an element?
options: It reduces opacity to 50%
It hides the element completely from visual display and screen readers
It moves the element off-screen to the right
It makes the element transparent but still clickable
questions.explanation: The hidden attribute indicates the element is not currently relevant and hides it from visual presentation and assistive tech.

questions.question: What does tabindex="0" do when applied to a <div> element?
options: It removes the element from keyboard focus entirely
It inserts the element into the natural keyboard tab navigation order
It forces the element to be the very first focused item upon page load
It disables all keyboard events
questions.explanation: tabindex="0" allows an element that is not naturally interactive (like a <div>) to receive keyboard focus in natural document order.
